Commentary: Nathan Smith to Tilak Varma, FOUR, short ball, Tilak swivels across, pulls it behind square and there's no one in the deep to cut it off. What a turnaround this is - just 17 needed now off 8 balls. Slipping away from New Zealand at the death
Nathan Smith to Tilak Varma, no run, comes charging down the pitch but ends up getting yorked by Smith who slants it away and beats him on the way to the keeper

Nathan Smith to Tilak Varma, SIX, the Indian players are on their feet in the dugout! They know all about what Tilak Varma can do and are watching another fine display from the left-hander here. Nerves of steel this guy. Slower length ball angled away wide of off, he hangs back, reaches out and slaps it over wide long-off for a remarkable six
Last over, 11 to get for India, and New Zealand have been penalised for their slow over-rate. Need an extra fielder in the ring
Jacob Duffy to Nitish Reddy, 1 run, banged in short, Reddy pulls hard but it goes straight to deep midwicket on the bounce
Santner, Duffy and Mitchell having a chat about the field. Square leg comes in the ring, mid-off is in, so is third man

Jacob Duffy to Tilak Varma, FOUR, full and wide, misses with his execution and Tilak absolutely blasts it away through extra cover. Might've been going for the wide yorker but ended up offering it right in the slot

Jacob Duffy to Tilak Varma, 2 runs, banged in short outside off, rushes Tilak on the pull and he mistimes it down to long-on. He was taking it a little easy on the second run, thinking the throw won't come to his end but then turned around and realised he had to put in the dive to make it back. Fifty up for him, job not done though
Jacob Duffy to Tilak Varma, 1 run, again he goes short outside off, Tilak doesn't get hold of it, cuts it in the air but it lands short of sweeper cover. Over to Reddy

Jacob Duffy to Nitish Reddy, wide, another bumper, goes past the attempted ramp, beating Reddy for pace but hang on ... the striker's end umpire feels it's too high. She spreads her arms to signal a wide. 2 needed off 2 - Duffy shakes his head as he walks back. Reddy was immediately asking for a wide and was searching to see where the umpire was. He looked at square leg but the ump was at point, giving the decision in his favour

Jacob Duffy to Nitish Reddy, 2 runs, remarkable turnaround here in Christchurch as India go 2-0 up in the series! Tilak Varma and Nitish Reddy the heroes for the visitors as they come back from nowhere to seal the win. Full toss on the pads, it's flicked away into the gap and they get back for two as the crowd erupts
Henry went off the field midway during that innings with some issue and couldn't complete his quota. Ferguson wasn't on the field for the last couple of overs either.

Santner 2/2: [On the batting effort and the partnerships between Bevon Jacobs and Glenn Phillips after losing early wickets] Obviously GP’s done it for a long time now, and I think even Bev, they played the situation beautifully. We lost three early and then they kind of built. I think we were only 60-odd after 10, but then I think it’s one of those surfaces where if you give yourself a chance, give yourself some balls, you can kind of cash in with the power of those two. I thought they played very well. And then, I mean, I blocked a couple of them, but Beast (Bracewell), you know, even 10 off two there to get us up to 180. [On Matt Henry being off the field and the possibility of injuries or rotation during the series] I think it’s precautionary, and I think Lockie went off as well. So hopefully those guys scrub up okay. But I think with the quick turnarounds throughout the series and in the one-days, there could be a bit of rotation. I think that’s just what it’s going to have to be.

Shreyas Iyer 2/2: [On India's fielding effort and the importance of preventing the opposition from taking twos] I think that was the message passed on to each and every player in the team, that you got to anticipate every ball that is coming to you, and just believe that you’re going to give singles, and just see to it that you’re running into the ball so that, you know, the opponents, they think twice about running twos. [On India's next destination and the team's progress in the series] Thank you so much. Job is still half done.

Under pressure with the odds against you, if there's one man you want in the middle it's Tilak Varma. Remarkable ability from the Hyderabad boy to deliver in crunch situations time and again, and today he just sneaked one out of the jaws of defeat for India. New Zealand will wonder what they have to do to get over the line against a team that just seems to have the wood over them. Next up we move from Christchurch to Wellington for the third T20I. Will see you there for all the action. For now, it's a goodbye from Sagar Chawla on behalf of Siva, Pradeep Krishnamurthy and Raju Peethala.
